newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore schools to promote national identity.
newsitem.headline: Singapore schools to promote national identity.

text.p: Singapore launched an island-wide education programme on Saturday aimed at teaching school children national identity and instilling a sense of pride.

Announcing a National Education initiative to all schools live on state television, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said the programme was designed to promote social cohesion and a national identity.
Lee said the programme was necessary because many Singaporeans, especially young people, knew little of the city-state's recent history, how it became an independent nation or became prosperous.

"This ignorance will hinder our effort to develop a shared sense of nationhood," Lee said. "For Singapore to thrive beyond the founder generation, we must systematically transmit these instincts and attitudes to succeeding cohorts."

Singapore was a British colony until the 1950s. It became self-governing in 1959 and joined the Federation of Malaysia in 1963, but split from its northern neighbour two years later to become fully independent.
The country has been dominated since independence by the People's Action Party, formed by Lee's father, Lee Kuan Yew.
The deputy prime minister said the National Education programme would be taught at all school levels, through formal and informal curriculums.
